Laura — thanks for the deck. Two quick asks from our side before we lock dates for the eval window: 1) can you confirm the tokens-per-dollar assumptions for our expected traffic profile (multi-turn clinical assistant, median turn length ~120 tokens); and 2) what caching model do you expect us to run for POC (prefix-only KV cache vs. session-level prefetch)?

Procurement also wants to understand whether batching will materially affect latency under our 95th percentile SLO (target <= 300ms p95 for single-turn prompts). We're happy to run a small sim but want Redwood's recommended operational knobs so our infra folks can provision appropriately.

Happy to discuss on Monday — Maya

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions clarifications

Maya — thanks for the questions, moving to clarify below and attaching a compact sim we ran against Acadia's sample profile (attached: token-econ-sim-20261003.pdf). Short answers up front: tokens/$ baseline = 9.3k tokens per USD for the hosted model variant we recommended (quantized, fp16 equivalent throughput); recommended cache = session-keyed KV prefix cache with 45% hit rate expectation for your interaction patterns; batching recommended for background inference and asynchronous flows (avg batch size 8), not for strict real-time single-turn where p95 latency matters.

Detailed assumptions we used in the sim (high level):
- Model: Redwood-Dialog-3.2 (q4_0k quant profile)
- Price assumption: $0.108 per 1k prompt+completion tokens (hosted list rate used for MAP economics) => ~9,260 tokens/USD
- Median turn length: 120 tokens; avg user session = 5 turns => 600 tokens/session
- Cache: prefix KV cache expecting 45% hit (based on repeated clinical templates and question overlap) => effective tokens billed per session drops to ~330 tokens/session
- Batching: for async journaling endpoints we assume continuous batching (size 8) yields ~22% token-cost benefit; for interactive single-turn endpoints we recommend batch=1 with micro-batching disabled to keep p95 under 300ms

Acceptance criteria we propose for MAP close:
1) Cost verification: POC run must demonstrate <= $0.75 median cost per session and <= $1.20 90th percentile cost per session across a 7-day controlled traffic test matching your sample distribution.
2) Latency: interactive route p95 <= 300ms for 95% of requests in production-like traffic; async route median latency <= 800ms with batching enabled.
3) Quality parity: automated eval (we'll run a 2k prompt eval set you supply) must not regress >2% on the clinical relevance metric vs. baseline.

Action items / next steps:
- We will send a MAP draft with milestone dates (PoC start, Eval window, Contract signoff) by EOD today.
- Can you share a 2k-prompt eval set (anonymized) and a 7-day traffic sample CSV?
- Procurement: if the cost acceptance criteria are met, can we align on a preferred billing cadence and lead time for Dedicated capacity?

I'll loop Rishi for any infra-level notes.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions clarifications

Hi Maya — quick infra clarifications from my side:
- The 45% cache-hit assumption is conservative for templated clinical dialogs; if you can increase client-side prefix normalization (strip PHI, canonicalize phrases) we typically see drift to ~55% which further reduces tokens billed.
- Batching: important distinction — server-side continuous batching (used on Redwood Hosted) helps throughput for background jobs; it doesn't increase single-request latency if we keep batch windows <=10ms and batch sizes small for interactive routes. For your p95 needs, we'll configure interactive routes with immediate dispatch (no artificial batch delay) and enable batching only on the async ingestion path.
- Quantization: q4_0k gives ~1.9-2.2x perf cost improvement vs fp16 in our runtime for conversational models; we recommend q4 for POC. If Acadia requires determinism/regression control we can pin a fp16 variant for Eval and compare quality vs q4 during the 2k eval run.

I'll prepare an infra runbook for the PoC that lists endpoints, expected peak RPS, batch windows, and KV cache TTLs. Sending that to the shared Drive link Laura mentioned.

-Rishi

Laura/Rishi — thanks, this is helpful. A couple clarifying points from product and procurement: 1) Procurement wants a worst-case unit cost if caching underperforms (we need a 95th percentile $/session number to model budget risk); 2) Product would like to see a short-run sim with q4 vs fp16 on our exact 500-sample representative set — can Redwood run that and share token counts and latency percentiles?

For procurement: if the 95th percentile cost per session (no-cache scenario) is <= $2.10 we can model the spend into our Q1 budget and move to an expedited procurement path. If that number is > $2.10 we'll need sign-off from finance which adds ~3 weeks. Can you include that worst-case in the MAP?

Thanks — Maya
